vision.title: A launchpad for student-led STEM work
vision.short: The NOVA STEM Leadership Club helps students turn an interest into a next step: a project, research experience, professional connection, public contribution, competition, or leadership role.
vision.promise: You joined because you want to become a STEM leader. Tell us where you want to go, and the club will help you find a path to get there.
model: Students choose a direction rather than waiting for an officer title.
The club supplies infrastructure: mentors, teammates, planning tools, introductions, logistics, and funding support when available.
Every active member can lead at an appropriate scale, from one meeting or outreach station to a semester-long research or technical project.
Students can combine pathways and move among them as their interests develop.

design_note: Competitions are treated as a way to practice leadership within several pathways, not as a pathway by themselves. Professional leadership and internal club leadership are separated so that mentoring, project management, and organizational stewardship remain visible.

action_modes.name: Explore
action_modes.description: Attend, observe, tour, or learn before making a larger commitment.

action_modes.name: Contribute
action_modes.description: Join a team and own a defined piece of work.

action_modes.name: Lead
action_modes.description: Set a goal, organize people and resources, and deliver an outcome.

action_modes.name: Represent
action_modes.description: Present, publish, compete, advocate, or speak for the club or a project.

action_modes.name: Mentor
action_modes.description: Help another student or a younger learner take a next step.

pathways.name: Community Outreach & Education
pathways.description: Help other people experience STEM through teaching, demonstrations, mentoring, and access-building.
pathways.student_outcomes: Facilitation, lesson design, volunteer coordination, mentoring, and inclusive public engagement.
example_activities: Lead a hands-on station at a K–12 STEM night
Build a reusable outreach kit and facilitator guide
Coordinate a tutoring or near-peer mentoring team
Host a career-exploration session for local students
Train club volunteers to deliver safe, accessible demonstrations

pathways.name: Research & Discovery
pathways.description: Ask questions, gather evidence, work with a mentor, and share findings.
pathways.student_outcomes: Research design, data practice, literature review, responsible conduct, posters, and presentations.
example_activities: Run a faculty research-match session
Form a small student research team
Hold a monthly paper or data discussion
Develop abstracts and posters for NCUR or a discipline meeting
Invite recent interns to explain how they found a lab

pathways.name: Engineering Design & Technical Projects
pathways.description: Build, test, debug, and improve something with a team.
pathways.student_outcomes: Scoping, systems thinking, technical documentation, safety, testing, iteration, and team delivery.
example_activities: Launch a rocketry, astronomy, robotics, or environmental-sensing project
Enter a cybersecurity, math-modeling, or NASA design challenge
Use the NOVA Fab Lab for a prototype sprint
Run a technical skills clinic led by students
Publish a build log and present lessons learned

pathways.name: Innovation & Entrepreneurship
pathways.description: Turn a real problem into a tested solution, venture, or community innovation.
pathways.student_outcomes: Problem discovery, customer interviews, prototyping, value propositions, pitching, and resource planning.
example_activities: Run a weekend design sprint around a campus or community problem
Host a founder or technology-transfer speaker
Build and test a minimum viable prototype
Prepare a pitch for the Community College Innovation Challenge
Map local incubators, makerspaces, and small-business resources

pathways.name: Career, Industry & Professional Leadership
pathways.description: Build a professional network, learn how STEM workplaces operate, and help peers prepare for the field.
pathways.student_outcomes: Networking, career planning, professional norms, team leadership, and understanding industry sectors.
example_activities: Organize a site visit, job-shadow day, or lab tour
Create a professional-society or student-chapter plan
Host a STEM alumni and employer roundtable
Lead a conference-preparation and networking workshop
Pair students for portfolio, résumé, and interview practice

pathways.name: Science Communication & Public Engagement
pathways.description: Make technical ideas clear, accurate, useful, and engaging for different audiences.
pathways.student_outcomes: Writing, speaking, visualization, storytelling, audience awareness, and responsible communication.
example_activities: Produce a student research showcase or lightning-talk night
Create a newsletter, podcast, video series, or explainer
Coach members for poster and oral presentations
Build a public exhibit around a local STEM issue
Translate a technical paper into a one-page community brief

pathways.name: Policy, Ethics & Civic Leadership
pathways.description: Connect evidence and technology with public decisions, ethics, regulation, and community needs.
pathways.student_outcomes: Policy research, ethical reasoning, stakeholder analysis, advocacy, and civic communication.
example_activities: Hold a briefing on a current AI, energy, health, space, or environmental issue
Attend a Washington-area science-policy event
Write a nonpartisan policy memo or public comment
Practice meeting with a policymaker or agency professional
Run an ethics case discussion tied to a club project

pathways.name: Peer & Organizational Leadership
pathways.description: Help people and projects succeed through mentoring, planning, stewardship, and a strong club culture.
pathways.student_outcomes: Mentoring, project management, meeting design, budgeting, fundraising, inclusion, and continuity.
example_activities: Mentor a new member through a first opportunity application
Manage a semester project calendar and team check-ins
Lead a funding request, sponsor proposal, or travel plan
Create a handoff kit for recurring club programs
Facilitate a retrospective and recognize member contributions

cadence.practice: Review deadlines in the next 45 days; post only items with a clear student action.
Assign members to verify a small batch of records against official pages and record the verification date.
Choose 6–10 priority opportunities, pair each with a club activity, and name a student opportunity captain.
Capture what the student applied for, attended, presented, or learned; save practical advice without storing sensitive application material.
Archive closed cycles, roll recurring opportunities forward only after dates are announced, and review the pathway framework with members.

roles.responsibility: Verifies official links, dates, prices, and status labels.
Curate 3–5 priority opportunities and one club activity for their pathway.
Run short clinics for résumés, abstracts, essays, and recommendation requests.
Maintains the middle- and high-school share list and connects competitions to mentoring.
Helps with institutional approvals, funding, risk, travel, and faculty introductions.

data_rules: Use a direct official program page, not a search result or third-party directory.
Never roll last year's date forward. Use TBA and keep last-cycle timing only in Notes.
Record the last verified date and a concrete next action for every active record.
Separate eligibility facts from recommendations; call out citizenship, age, GPA, enrollment, and transfer-status limits.
Archive rather than delete major recurring opportunities so students can plan early for the next cycle.
